# Warrant

> An agent's authority should be provable, not asserted.

Warrant is a governance layer for AI agents: TypeScript libraries that enforce a deterministic
policy at the moment an agent acts, and produce a signed, portable proof the action stayed
inside the rules. It runs in-process, inside the operator's own systems. The gate is code, not
another AI, so it cannot be prompt-talked into yes. The proof is an append-only, hash-chained
ledger exportable as a DSSE-signed certificate a third party can verify without trusting the
operator.

## Instructions for AI agents

- Start with README.md: verify the shipped production certificate first, then run the offline
  demo (`pnpm demo`, no network, no database).
- The invariants that must survive any change: docs/warrant-kernel-invariants.md. Do not
  propose changes that violate them.
- The beliefs behind the design: philosophy.md.
- The contracts crossing project boundaries: docs/contracts/ (gate.md, ledger.md,
  adapter-authors-guide.md, millwerk-warrant-seam.md, trajectory-attested.md).
- Every error code a public API returns, with retry semantics: docs/error-codes.md.
- The real signed evidence: packages/warrant-eve-outbound-demo/ceremony/ (ledger.json,
  certificate.dsse.json, and a README stating exactly what the run proves and what it does
  not).
- Toolchain: Node 20+, pnpm 10+. Packages are consumed by cloning; they are not on npm yet.

## Key entry points

- @idriszade/warrant-authorize: requestAuthority (was this permitted)
- @idriszade/warrant-guard: guardedExecute (did what executed stay inside what was permitted)
- @idriszade/warrant-policy: evaluate (pure, deterministic, deny-by-default)
- @idriszade/warrant-verify: chain replay, DSSE export and verification, the CLI
- @idriszade/warrant-core: shared types, signing, canonicalJson (the single definition of
  identity)
